newsitem.title: USA: Outplacement firm sees job growth in NY metro area.
newsitem.headline: Outplacement firm sees job growth in NY metro area.

text.p: Companies in the New York metropolitan area are expected to increase hiring in 1997, especially firms in financial services, pharmaceuticals and information technology, an outplacment firm said on Monday.
But this does not mean that selective pruning will not remain a factor in one of New York City's most important sectors, Wall Street brokerage houses.

"While there will still be layoffs in the securities industry, as under-achievers and non-performers are replaced, overall there will be strong net job gains consistent with 1996," said Barbara Barra, senior vice president at Lee Hecht Harrison, in prepared remarks. She cited industry estimates that the sector created over 10,000 jobs in 1996.
The company, which has offices throughout the U.S. and in Europe, said it was the third largest outplacement company in the world.
One of the rosiest areas in the metropolitan region will continue to be systems and information technology, Barra predicted.

The outlook is less robust, however, for the healthcare industry, though pharaceuticals companies are expected to remain strong. "Stricter reimbursement policies and other bottom-line concerns will force continued staff reductions throughout the industry," she said.
And job creation is expected to be dominated by smaller, local companies than large, national and international firms, which increasingly are outsourcing secondary functions.
